subject: Commercial onramp and procurement path — Orbit Analytics trial next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@orbit-analytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.inference, marissa_cole@redwood.inference
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial onramp and procurement path — Orbit Analytics trial next steps

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on procurement and the trial -> paid path. Notes pulled from the call below.

Key items we agreed / flagged
- Procurement path: Orbit preference currently seems to be PO via centralized procurement, but you mentioned interest in AWS Marketplace as an alternate path for faster provisioning.
- Trial start target: you suggested early June (we discussed June 1).
- Success criteria: you want a combination of integration stability and throughput — test target is to validate 3 production flows (inference pipelines) and demonstrate sustained throughput that meets latency SLOs.
- Acceptance thresholds to confirm: 99th pct latency below 800ms for typical single-turn requests; end-to-end throughput target ~5k inference calls/day for the initial cohort (we can tighten these once we get telemetry).
- Commercial path options: card for initial smoke test (small spend) vs PO for trial and billing.

Attachments I’m including for procurement & trial planning:
- [attachment: Redwood_Sales_SOW_v1.pdf] (draft SOW / trial scope)
- [attachment: trial-acceptance-criteria.xlsx] (suggested pass/fail metrics we discussed)

Proposed next steps
1) You share the Orbit PO template (or procurement contact) so we can confirm contract terms and payment timing.
2) We can provision a sandbox environment immediately; if you want a rapid smoke test we can accept a corporate card for a small initial run to validate integrations before the PO is in place.
3) If you prefer marketplace, I’ll pull the listing link and pricing export for your procurement team.
4) Laura (CC) will own onboarding and success plan; she’ll propose a milestone schedule once we lock the start date.

Can you confirm: (A) preferred procurement path (PO -> net-30 vs AWS Marketplace vs card for smoke test), (B) target billing effective date if PO is used, and (C) who in procurement should I loop in?

If it helps, I’m free Monday 11–1pm PT to do a short sync with Procurement + Engineering.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Orbit live.

—
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[attachment: Redwood_Sales_SOW_v1.pdf]
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@orbit-analytics.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference>
Cc: Calvin Park <calvin.park@orbit-analytics.com>
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial onramp and procurement path — Orbit Analytics trial next steps

Diego —

Appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers from procurement side:
- Procurement: Our canonical path is a PO (Net 30) issued by our Central Procurement team. PO will need our standard redlines; terms and insurance need review.
- Marketplace: Procurement likes marketplace because it's simpler and reduces contract friction, but they need to see the same billing/usage visibility and a comparable SLO in writing.
- Card: We can approve a corporate card for a small smoke test (up to $500) for initial integration verification.
- Target start: We’re aiming to start formal trial activity on 2026-06-01. Procurement expects to have a PO to you by 2026-05-25 if all internal approvals go smoothly.

I’m attaching our PO template for your contracts team to sanity-check.

[attachment: Orbit_PO_Template.pdf]

Success criteria — from our side we’ll measure:
- Integration stability: no more than 2 production-impacting errors in the first 2 weeks.
- Latency: 95th pct < 700ms and 99th pct < 1s for production payloads (we can start with the 800ms number you proposed and tighten to this if needed).
- Usage: reach 100k inference tokens within 30 days of start, and demonstrate predictable token consumption patterns.

I’ll cc Procurement (Calvin) on the PO once we confirm SOW and marketplace vs PO choice.

Talk soon —
Samantha
Sr. Product Ops Manager | Orbit Analytics
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@orbit-analytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.inference, marissa_cole@redwood.inference
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial onramp and procurement path — Orbit Analytics trial next steps

Thanks Samantha — this is great and helpful. Short reply with options to make progress quickly:

Option A (fastest): Card-enabled smoke test this week/month — use corporate card (up to $500) to run the integration and sanity checks. We’ll provision keys and a short onboarding: 1 hour tech sync + sample integration guide. No billing until you flip the toggle.

Option B (preferred by Procurement): Start formal trial on June 1 tied to your PO. We can align start-of-billing with the PO effective date; if procurement needs a SOW + terms in place before issuing PO we’ll move through that track.

Option C (Marketplace): If Procurement wants marketplace, we’ll provide the AWS Marketplace listing + pricing exports. Note: Marketplace often means different invoicing cadence and may require a workbook from your procurement team to map SKUs.

Regarding acceptance criteria and telemetry, I’ve attached the trial-acceptance-criteria spreadsheet with the thresholds you outlined and also included recommended signal hooks we’ll provide in the Console (token usage, per-route latency, error rate, cold-start indicators).

Next steps I’ll take now:
- Share Marketplace listing link (if you want) + pricing export.
- Send a narrow SOW with trial dates and milestone schedule for Procurement review (based on Redwood_Sales_SOW_v1.pdf).
- Schedule the onboarding call with Laura to lock the 1-hour tech sync.

Laura — could you propose two slots on Mon/Tue next week for the onboarding session?

Diego
[attachment: trial-acceptance-criteria.xlsx]

Subject: Onboarding & success plan for Orbit Analytics trial

Hi Samantha / Diego —

Thanks — happy to own the onboarding and success plan. Short plan below (we’ll tailor after the initial sync):

Week 0 (pre-trial)
- Prep: confirm test dataset, ingest sample payloads, generate API keys.
- Security review: confirm network egress rules and any IP allowlist requirements.

Day 1 (kickoff)
- 1-hour tech session: walkthrough SDKs, quick integration, and data retention settings.
- Smoke tests: run 10 sample flows against the sandbox.

Week 1–2
- Production pilot: validate three production flows, monitor latency and error rate.
- Weekly check-ins (15m) and dashboard access.

Success criteria to gate paid conversion (aligns with Diego’s doc, Samantha’s asks)
- Integration stability: <2 P0/P1 incidents during pilot window.
- Latency: 95th <700ms, 99th <1s (or mutually agreed revised numbers).
- Usage baseline: >=100k tokens processed within 30 days for the pilot group.

Deliverables we’ll provide
- Daily token + latency report for the pilot cohort
- One consolidated runbook for production cutover
- Checklist for Procurement / Legal to streamline PO signing

Please reply with who on your engineering side will own the integration so we can send calendar invites.

—
Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@orbit-analytics.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference>, laura_bennett@redwood.inference
Cc: Calvin Park <calvin.park@orbit-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 14:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial onramp and procurement path — Orbit Analytics trial next steps

Diego / Laura —

All good from our side. Final confirmations:
- Preferred procurement path: PO (Net 30) for the formal trial and subsequent subscription. Procurement still prefers marketplace but given timeline they’ll issue a PO for the pilot. Calvin (procurement) will own the PO — I’ve CC’d him.
- PO timeline: Procurement will aim to route the PO to Redwood by 2026-05-25.
- Interim smoke test: We will run a card-based smoke test this week with our engineering lead (Eve Park) — limited to $500. This is to validate integration only.
- Trial start: Formal trial start = 2026-06-01. We want billing aligned with the PO effective date; if the PO effective date is later we’ll discuss backdating or credit mechanics.

Requests for you:
1) Please send the AWS Marketplace listing link and pricing export (so Calvin can confirm marketplace parity).
2) Please send the final SOW as a PDF we can attach to the PO.

We’ll expect the PO and any procurement follow-ups from Calvin; Diego, if you can send the marketplace link and the SOW PDF today that would be ideal. Laura, please send calendar invites for the 1-hour onboarding tech sync.

Thanks —
Samantha
Sr. Product Ops Manager | Orbit Analytics
